# Tb022 — Tolerance declared in different units than coordinates

## Sources
- synthesized time-bomb (Pass F).

## Description

A file's `LENGTH_UNIT` declared in `GEOMETRIC_REPRESENTATION_CONTEXT` is `.MILLI..METRE.` (mm). The `UNCERTAINTY_MEASURE_WITH_UNIT` uses a *different* inline `LENGTH_UNIT` of `.METRE.` (m), with value 1e-6 — that is, 1e-6 m = 1e-3 mm. A kernel that interprets the uncertainty in the context's units (mm) reads "1e-6 mm = 1 nm — hyper-precise". A kernel that follows the uncertainty's own attached unit reads "1e-6 m = 1 µm = 1000× looser". The receiver's policy on which unit binding to follow determines a 1000× difference in working tolerance — every other defect in this section becomes a different defect class.

## Reproducer recipe

Two `LENGTH_UNIT` records — one bound to the `GEOMETRIC_REPRESENTATION_CONTEXT` (mm), one bound to the `UNCERTAINTY_MEASURE_WITH_UNIT` (m). Coordinates in mm.

## Expected kernel behavior

unit-binding policy for tolerance must be documented; the spec attaches each `UNCERTAINTY_MEASURE_WITH_UNIT` to its own unit, so receivers must convert before comparing to coordinates.
